NONE: › (the hollow stem of) any of various types of tall, stiff plants like grasses growing together in groups near water
蘆葦（稈）
› a thin piece of wood or metal that vibrates very quickly to produce sound in a musical instrument when someone blows it
（吹奏樂器的）簧片，簧舌
› a musical instrument, such as the clarinet or oboe, that produces sound when a musician blows on the reed
簧樂器（如單簧管、雙簧管等）
› A reedy place has many reeds (= tall plants like grass).
蘆葦叢生的；長滿蘆葦的
› disapproving A reedy sound, especially a voice, is thin and high and not pleasant to listen to.
（尤指嗓音）尖細刺耳的，尖厲難聽的

example: the reedy river banks
蘆葦叢生的河岸

NONE: › a line of rocks or sand just above or just below the surface of the sea, often dangerous to ships
礁；暗礁；礁脈

example: a dangerous offshore reef
靠近岸邊的危險暗礁
a coral reef
珊瑚礁

NONE: › a type of strong knot that is tied twice and cannot easily be unfastened
平結

C: › old-fashioned informal a cigarette that you roll yourself containing the drug cannabis
› also reefer jacket a jacket made of thick material and often worn by sailors

NONE: › to have a strong unpleasant smell
發出臭味；發出難聞的氣味

example: Her breath reeked of garlic.
她一吐氣就有一股難聞的大蒜味。

NONE: › If an event or situation reeks of an unpleasant quality, it seems to be caused by or connected to that quality.
明顯帶有，充滿（令人不快的特性）

example: His promotion reeks of favouritism.
他的升職明顯有偏向的成分在內。

C: › a round, wheel-shaped object on which sewing thread, fishing wire, film, etc. can be rolled, or the amount of thread, etc. stored on one of these
捲軸；捲筒；捲盤；繞在捲軸上的線
› a fast Scottish or Irish dance, or the music for this
裡爾舞（一種輕快的蘇格蘭或愛爾蘭舞蹈）；裡爾舞曲

NONE: › to walk, moving from side to side, looking like you are going to fall
踉蹌；打趔趄；蹣跚；搖搖晃晃地挪動
› If the place where you are reels, what you are looking at seems to go round and round in front of you.
仿佛天旋地轉
› If you reel, or your mind or brain reels, you feel very confused or shocked and unable to act.
發蒙；感到眩暈

example: At closing time he reeled out of the bar and fell down on the pavement.
酒吧關門時，他踉踉蹌蹌走了出來，一跤摔在人行道上。
She hit him so hard that he reeled backwards.
她出手太重，打得他朝後打了個趔趄。
A stone hit his head and the street reeled before his eyes.
一塊石頭砸在他頭上，他頓時覺得街道在他眼前打旋。
We were reeling (in amazement/shock/delight, etc.) from/with the news that we had won all that money.
得知贏了那麽多錢，我們都（驚愕得／震驚得／高興得）發蒙了。

NONE: › mainly US to get control of something or someone, sometimes by offering something in exchange
（透過交易）控制（某人或某事）

example: The article offers tips on how computer users can avoid being reeled in by internet scams.
這篇文章給了電腦用戶一些指點，讓他們避免成為網路騙局的受害者。

NONE: › to pull in a rope or an object on the end of a rope by turning a wheel round and round, or to release something in the same way
繞動捲軸把…收起／放開

example: Slowly the fisherman reeled in his line, bringing the fish ashore.
垂釣者慢慢收繞魚線，把魚拉到岸上。
The firefighters reeled out the hoses from their fire engine.
消防員從消防車上把水龍帶放出來。

NONE: › informal to say a long list of things quickly and without stopping
一口氣說出；滔滔不絕地講
› US informal to win several games or points one after the other in a sports competition
（體育比賽中）接連獲勝，連連得分

example: The old man reeled off the names of his 22 grandchildren.
老人一口氣說出了他22個孫子孫女的名字。
